home.eyebrow: ElivCloud · a personal project by Elena Shlenskova
home.heading: Exploring complex systems, people and technology.
home.intro: ElivCloud is my evolving personal project. It brings together more than 15 years of legal practice, my knowledge of social psychology, conflict and negotiation, a growing technical practice in applied AI and automation, and personal experiments with new tools.
home.supporting_text: I am interested in how complex problems actually work: where interests and risks lie, how people make decisions, how knowledge becomes a process, and how an idea can be developed into a working system. This site is a space for completed projects, experiments and new directions that gradually form a larger picture.

directions.title: Law and finance
directions.text: Transactions, corporate and project finance, contractual structures, risk and complex multi-party processes.

directions.title: Conflict and negotiation
directions.text: Interests and positions, conflict dynamics, negotiation strategies, mediation and the human context behind decisions.

directions.title: Applied AI and automation
directions.text: AI assistants, knowledge retrieval, information processing, automation and decision support designed to remain transparent and human-controlled.

directions.title: Projects and experiments
directions.text: From complete working services to smaller explorations of multimodality, third-party APIs and new ways of interacting with technology.

home.featured_intro: Completed systems in which an idea moves from a domain problem and architecture to an interface, testing and a working deployment.
home.closing_heading: I do not see the human and the technical as opposites.
home.closing_text: The interesting work begins where they meet — and where observations can become ideas, experiments and working projects.

about.meta_description: About Elena Shlenskova: legal practice, finance, conflict and negotiation, applied AI, project implementation and technical experimentation.
about.heading: About me
about.intro: I rarely look at a problem through the lens of a single discipline. Legal practice taught me to see structure, risk and interdependence; conflict and negotiation drew my attention to interests, behaviour and interaction; technology offers a way to turn ideas into working systems.

sections.title: Law, transactions and finance
sections.body: I have more than 15 years of legal experience, focused on corporate and project finance, international transactions and legal support for business. This work taught me to navigate ambiguity, identify material risks, structure information and keep the whole problem in view.

sections.title: People, conflict and negotiation
sections.body: Alongside law, I have a long-standing interest in social psychology, conflict, negotiation and mediation. Formal rules are rarely enough in a complex situation: it also matters to understand the participants' interests, the dynamics between them, the reasons behind resistance and how decisions are actually made.

sections.title: Technology and automation
sections.body: My interest in applied AI began with a practical question: how can technology reduce routine work without losing context, accountability or human judgement? I am now building hands-on experience with AI systems, Python, backend development, automation, knowledge retrieval and data workflows.

sections.title: Projects and implementation
sections.body: I am interested not only in the idea, but in taking it to a working state: designing the structure, data, interface, safeguards, tests, security and deployment approach.

sections.title: Curiosity and experimentation
sections.body: Not every project has to solve a large business problem. Sometimes a project is a way to test an idea, understand a tool or explore a different form of interaction. This is where my experiments with multimodality, third-party APIs and generative scenarios belong.

about.closing: I am less interested in choosing between the human and the technical than in exploring what emerges where they meet.

expertise.meta_description: Law and finance, social psychology and negotiation, applied AI and digital system implementation — the connected areas of Elena Shlenskova's work.
expertise.heading: Areas of work
expertise.intro: The same approach connects these areas: understand the real problem, see the people, risks and dependencies involved, and then design a solution that can be explained and implemented.

pillars.title: Law, transactions and finance
pillars.description: Legal and transactional work with complex structures, multiple participants and decisions that must align legal, financial and operational requirements.

pillars.title: Social psychology, conflict and negotiation
pillars.description: Understanding interests and positions, interaction dynamics and the human context that shapes decisions, agreements and the development of conflict.

pillars.title: Applied AI and automation
pillars.description: Systems that help retrieve, classify, summarise and route information while preserving transparency, control and the ability to examine how a result was reached.

pillars.title: System design and implementation
pillars.description: Turning a domain problem into a complete working process — from architecture, data and interfaces to testing, infrastructure and deployment.

expertise.closing_text: Whatever the domain, I begin with the same questions: what is really happening, whose interests are involved, where risk appears, what information is missing and what would make the next decision clearer.

experience.meta_description: Elena Shlenskova's experience across legal practice, negotiation, applied AI and complete digital systems.
experience.heading: Experience
experience.intro: My experience is made up of several connected strands. Some have developed over many years, while others are newer, but today they reinforce one another.

stages.title: Legal practice and business support
stages.text: More than 15 years of work with contracts, transactions, risk and decisions that require precision, accountability and an understanding of the real business context. The work involves looking beyond the formal requirement to understand how it affects the transaction structure, the participants and the decisions that follow.

stages.title: Corporate and project finance
stages.text: Experience with complex financing structures, international elements, multiple participants and documentation that must remain internally coherent. This context requires legal, financial and operational dependencies — and the effect of any change on the overall structure — to remain visible at the same time.

stages.title: Conflict, negotiation and the human factor
stages.text: Knowledge of social psychology, conflict, negotiation and mediation helps me look beyond formal positions to the interests involved, the dynamics between participants and the reasons decisions move forward or become blocked. This perspective is especially useful where formal positions alone do not explain resistance, delay or mismatched expectations.

stages.title: Applied AI and automation
stages.text: Hands-on development of AI assistants, triage systems, knowledge retrieval, reporting, automation and structured information processing. Across these projects, I pay particular attention to context, transparency and keeping people in control of the final decision.

stages.title: Complete digital solutions
stages.text: Building working systems rather than isolated prompts, including APIs, databases, interfaces, authentication, tests, security, Docker deployment and audit trails. For me, a solution should go beyond a demonstration and hold up when tested against data, tests and a real user workflow.

stages.title: Continuous learning and experimentation
stages.text: Learning new tools through personal projects, from production-style services to smaller explorations of multimodality, third-party APIs and generative scenarios. Experiments make it possible to test a hypothesis quickly, understand a tool's limitations and decide whether an idea is worth developing further.
